title: Commanders of Attention 2: The Magnetizers
coreMove: Hold attention by opening a personally relevant or unfinished loop that the later message can legitimately close.
sourcePressure: The source identifies self-relevant, unfinished, and mysterious cues as magnetizers that hold attention long enough for later association and persuasion.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Create suspense or mystery regardless of whether it serves the choice.

hook: An abstract claim that attention changes everything
A generic meeting where someone makes a better pitch
A clever sentence about persuasion before any concrete object appears
counterintuition: You think persuasion happens during the ask, but it happens before it
The obvious factor is not always the important one
Influence is not manipulation when used well
tryThisNow: Set a timer and reflect on attention
Write down three ways to be more persuasive
Ask yourself what matters most right now

exampleSpecs.audience: a policy designer trying to keep homeowners reading
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether self-relevance holds attention past the first paragraph
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the designer opens with the customer’s street flood-zone change, then reveals the premium options
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a renewal letter with the street name in the first line

exampleSpecs.audience: a studio mentor keeping students engaged with unfinished designs
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether an unresolved edge holds attention better than a completed rendering
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the mentor covers the final rendering and leaves the unresolved stair section visible while students predict the fix
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a half-pinned floor plan curling at one corner

exampleSpecs.audience: a retail trainer teaching associates to notice greeting gaps
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether a mystery queue keeps attention through a dull protocol
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the trainer shows three anonymous receipts and asks which visit lost the shopper before revealing the greeting note
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three receipts clipped to a cork strip

exampleSpecs.audience: a volunteer coordinator explaining why incomplete records matter
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether unfinished information keeps volunteers tracking the animal past intake
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator leaves one field blank on a rescued hawk card and asks what treatment becomes impossible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a hawk intake card beside a taped carrier

exampleSpecs.audience: a trial consultant helping jurors follow a timeline
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether mystery should be opened only where evidence can close it
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the consultant withholds the final timestamp until jurors have marked the unexplained gap themselves
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a timeline board with one empty timestamp slot

exampleSpecs.audience: a service designer trying to retain users ethically
exampleSpecs.stakes: whether an unfinished setup checklist holds attention without trapping the user
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the designer removes the false progress bar and keeps only the real unfinished data export task
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a cancellation screen with one unchecked export box

skillTargets: close mystery with evidence rather than suspense
notice when held attention becomes manipulative

tryThisNowSpec: Turn one dull request into an honest open loop by naming a personally relevant unanswered question that the request will actually resolve.
